radiopost_vectors: Forms: templates, fingerprints, a form's text and its values checked
rule: Each template file becomes exactly `canonical_hex` (RP-2 §8.1) and has the fingerprint `fingerprint_hex`. The named message (messages.json) shows as `text` with its template and as `text_without_template` without it (§8.4). Each check's `values`, against ICS-213, give `expect`: `fills the template`, or why not (§8.2).

every_type.rule: `template` becomes exactly `canonical_hex` (RP-2 §8.1) and has the fingerprint `fingerprint_hex`. Each of `messages` shows as `text` with the template and as `text_without_template` without it (§8.4). Each of `values_shown` is the value of the template's field `field`, written `shown` (§8.4; a `rows` value's lines joined by LF). Each check's `values` give `expect`: `fills the template`, or why not (§8.2). Each of `templates` keeps §8.1's rules (`keeps the rules`) or is not a template, `expect` saying which rule it breaks. In JSON a map's keys are its numbers written as text.
